stances.summary: Uses baseball metaphor to discuss constitutional law implications

stances.summary: Criticizes judicial deference to presidential invasion claims
stances.quote: Today, en banc 5th Circuit dismissed key Alien Enemies Act case on procedural grounds. See my linked post for details. I also critique a dubious concurring opinion in which Judge James Ho advocates absolute deference to president's claims that an "invasion" has occurred: reason.c

stances.summary: Notes Sotomayor's rising popularity reflects issue salience shifts
stances.quote: Sotomayor has impressive +10 net approval ratings in recent surveys (though much of public has no opinion). Even I am more favorable to her now, because of growing prominence of issues she's good on (e.g. - immigration),  rather than bad (e.g. property rights). Trump has Made Sot

stances.summary: Notes public approval data showing justices less unpopular than Trump/Congress
stances.quote: The data also show most people know little or nothing about individual justices. But Sotomayor is the most popular justice, and  Thomas the least. Yet even Thomas has far less bad net approval ratings than Trump and Congress.

stances.summary: Supreme Court public support matters for defending judicial review
stances.quote: In this post, I consider recent data showing Supreme Court is only modestly unpopular and most of its major recent rulings have majority support. This says little about quality of Court's work, but relevant to protecting judicial review against threats from right and left: reason

stances.summary: Argues Trump's birthright citizenship order is unconstitutional
stances.quote: In this post, I explain why most of Trump's new executive order targeting birthright citizenship is blatantly unconstitutional under the Supreme Court's recent ruling in Trump v. Barbara: reason.com/volokh/2026/...

stances.summary: Offers qualified critique of Supreme Court's recent decisions
stances.quote: My qualified endorsement of @davidcole-gtown.bsky.social's insightful qualified defense of the Supreme Court's recent work (read and you will see why there's 2 levels of qualification here; I think he's sometimes too nice to the Court, sometimes the opposite): reason.com/volokh/2

stances.summary: Defends judicial review as check on executive power
stances.quote: As explained in my article, the Court has in fact blocked multiple Republican executive power grabs. Destroying judicial review would only make such moves much easier. And the court doesn’t prevent Congress from cutting back executive power in all sorts of ways, if it wants to.

stances.summary: Disputes characterization of proposal as court-packing
stances.quote: I didn’t cheer it. But it’s not court-packing.

stances.summary: Defines court-packing as size increase for ideological change
stances.quote: Court-packing is increasing the size of the court in order to to change its ideological balance. Craig proposes exactly that and says so. He also wants to then reverse it with a term limit amendment.

stances.summary: Defends courts' track record of constraining executive overreach across administrations
stances.quote: They aren’t perfect. But have done it many times before, including just recently in multiple Trump-constraining cases I listed. Also in giving Biden broad leeway on immigration and cracking down on red-state social media restrictions.

stances.summary: Opposes court-packing as dangerous solution despite acknowledging proposal's creativity
stances.quote: In this new @theunpopulist.net article I respond to @andycraig.bsky.social's defense of court-packing. His proposal is better and more creative than standard packing plans, but still a dangerous cure worse than the disease it seeks to treat:  www.theunpopulist.net/p/court-pack...

stances.summary: Opposes Trump's Section 338 tariffs as harmful, illegal, and damaging to allied relations

stances.summary: Opposes Trump's Section 301 tariffs as harmful and illegal

stances.summary: Highlights legal vulnerabilities in Trump's Section 338 tariffs

stances.summary: Highlights legal challenges to Trump's Section 301 tariffs

stances.summary: Criticizes Trump tariffs for damaging US credibility; proposes court and Congressional remedies

stances.summary: Opposes Trump's Section 301 tariffs, supports legal challenges

stances.summary: Opposes Trump's Section 301 tariffs, supports legal challenges

stances.summary: Argues Section 301 tariffs are illegal

stances.summary: Opposes mass deportation, argues larger migrant numbers strengthen case against it
